❯ Without using any tools, write a 40-line poem about terminal multiplexers.

◆ In one dark window, many lives awake,
  A shell divides itself for work's sake,
  With panes like rooms along a quiet hall,
  Each prompt a lantern hung upon the wall.
  Tmux keeps the session when the wire is gone,
  Through sudden drops the distant tasks live on,
  The laptop shuts, the server does not sleep,
  Its buffers hold what scattered hands would keep.
  Screen, elder sibling, plain and tried by years,
  Still guards the login past our doubts and fears,
  While newer hosts arrange their tabs in rows,
  And names each window where the cargo goes.
  A prefix key is struck, then c or n,
  A pane is born, then split and split again,
  Left runs the build, the right edits the code,
  Below, the logs rehearse what errors showed.
  Here vim is dreaming in a column bright,
  There htop paints the CPU in light,
  A test suite mutters, counting pass and fail,
  And tail keeps following a lengthening tale.
  Detach is mercy when the network bends,
  Attach is homecoming that never ends,
  No process begs the terminal to stay,
  The session holds them when we walk away.
  Copy the scrollback, search the vanished line,
  A thousand outputs frozen still in time,
  The mouse may wander, keys may take command,
  Each border answers to a practiced hand.
  One window watches, one begins to deploy,
  One holds a shell we keep just to enjoy,
  And multiplexed, the single screen grows wide,
  With parallel lives laboring side by side.
  It is a harbour built of text and light,
  For ships of process sailing through the night,
  No storm of logout tears them from their berth,
  They ride in memory, snug against the earth.
  So bless the daemon, patient, spare, and true,
  That folds a dozen terminals in two,
  Or three, or twenty, neat in one display —
  And waits, reattached, at the break of day.
